intended_object: The canonical map sending a tuple of elements (x_i) ∈ ∏_i |D_i| to the element of the indexed product neighbourhood system |∏_i D_i| whose neighbourhoods are the finite-support cylinders ∏_i X_i with X_i ∈ x_i. It is the inverse half of Scott's isomorphism |∏ D_i| ≅ ∏ |D_i| (infinitary Prop. 3.2, Exercise 6.29). Inferred from the docstring and its use as invFun of iprodEquiv.
explanation: Membership: W is in fromPi D x exactly when W = iprodNbhd X for a tuple X with X i ∈ x i for all i and finite support (FinSupp D X). This is the intended filter of cylinders. It matches the neighbourhoods of iprod D (cylinders of D_i-neighbourhoods that are the master outside finitely many coordinates), restricted to coordinates lying in each x i. The element axioms are all checked coordinatewise: sub follows because each x i is an element; master_mem uses the all-master tuple with empty support; inter_mem uses iprodNbhd_inter and FinSupp.inter; up_mem uses iprodNbhd_subset_iff and upward closure in each x i. The file proves proj (fromPi D x) i = x i and fromPi D (proj z ·) = z, so this is the correct inverse of the order isomorphism. Using a List as the finite-support witness is equivalent to the support being a finite set. The only artifact: the section variable [DecidableEq ι] is probably included in the signature although the body never uses it. Classically every type has decidable equality, so this costs no real generality. The construction is stated for an arbitrary index type and arbitrary families of neighbourhood systems, its natural generality. Mathlib has no theory of Scott neighbourhood systems, so there is no counterpart.
